It had been a while since the Simple Equation had been discovered. Its application had yielded many uses, mainly for war. One in particular stood out: the cannon. The basic cannon the Deva developed was simple: stone, carved into a tube closed at one end with a small hole for a fuse to be inserted, with a metal projectile. Of course, this was not good enough for the warlike people. The stone cannons kept exploding, and that was a big no-no. Banding was experimented with - all it served to do was keep the banded areas form exploding and nothing else. The tried thickening the walls, but that made them overly heavy and obnoxious to aim, to the point where they only had any use as stationary artillery designed to hit one spot repeatedly and nowhere else. Wooden barrels simply vaporized on ignition. Finally, a solution was found. Cast iron barrels blended durability and mobility to form a deadly combination. The thickness of the barrels was a problem for a while - too thin and they turned to shrapnel bombs, (which the scientists enthusiastically noted for later study) too thick and they had the same problems the stone cannons did, but to a lesser degree. The sweet spot was finally found, and emplacements went up all around the mountain.
